title: Piyush's Applied Philosophy Reels
content: Piyush creates short Instagram Reels using philosophical texts and characters as lenses for applied philosophy. The style is punchy and dense, blending stoicism, mental models, and critical thinking. He also uses a 90s cel-shaded anime aesthetic for certain reels. Principles include audience-first hooks, specificity over abstraction, and binary polls tied to the video's content. The pipeline involves concept, scripting, recording/editing, and upload optimization. Fixed hashtags include #stoicism, #criticalthinking, #selfimprovement, #mentalmodels, and #deepthinking. Creative block involves feeling unqualified and holding back on certain content due to fear of misinterpretation. Possible future hooks include a reel about stopping to wait for qualification and a Nolan adaptation of *Odyssey*. Claude is used for extraction, tightening, and polish, steering Piyush back to audience growth when he drifts inward. Source material includes Stoic texts, Bhagavad Gita, and Homeric epics.
raw_text:
- Short talking-head reels using Marcus Aurelius, Krishna, Odysseus as perceptual lenses. Positioned as applied philosophy, not self-help. Aim is to shift how people see things
- Draws on stoicism, mental models, intentional living, critical thinking. Style is punchy and dense
- Also short reels with a 90s cel-shaded anime aesthetic (teleportation and identity, hedonic adaptation)
- Principles: audience-first hooks, specificity over abstraction, one reference and one punchline per reel, binary polls tied to the video's content
- Pipeline: concept, scripting, recording/editing, upload optimization. Fixed hashtags: #stoicism #criticalthinking #selfimprovement #mentalmodels #deepthinking
- Creative block: feels unqualified while his life feels disordered. Planned reel: "Stop waiting to be qualified". Holding back on Krishna-Arjuna content for fear of misinterpretation. A Nolan *Odyssey* adaptation is a possible hook
- Uses Claude for extraction, tightening and polish, not wholesale generation. Wants to be steered back to audience-growth thinking when he drifts inward. Source material: Stoic texts, Bhagavad Gita, Homeric epics
